_source.cutoff: author date before 2026-10-26T00:00:00-07:00 (through 25 October 2026, Owen's local time)
commands: git -C <repo> log <branch> --before=2026-10-26T00:00:00-07:00 --format='%ad' --date=short | sort -u | wc -l   (local-time day count, for cross-reference)

workspace/1026/count-commits.js in the working repo does all of the above in one pass (read-only git, no fetch, no checkout); run with the 12 Oct cutoff it reproduces the 12 Oct atlas, portal and Quartz blocks field for field (workspace/1026/project-block.js check).
notes: All buckets use the AUTHOR date converted to UTC. Owen commits from UTC-07:00, so a late-evening local commit lands on the next UTC day (a commit at 22:41 local is bucketed on the next UTC day). The local-time span and day count are carried alongside in each project's "local_time" block because the site copy quotes local dates.

Atlas is measured on `origin/master`, the production branch, as it stands in the local clone without a fetch: a94f97f4, last commit 14 Oct 2026, 2,738 commits. On 12 Oct origin/master was c0515922 (2,720). Run today with the 12 Oct cutoff, origin/master gives 2,724, because 4 commits from the `next` branch, committed before 12 Oct, reached production afterwards; the series moves to the current ref. The 16 commits on `next` that are not on origin/master are not counted. Local `main` (9 Sep) and local `master` (21 Aug) are stale and were NOT used.

Quartz, Mantle, Helm and six smaller repos went public between 20 and 23 Oct. Each public history is a re-rooted copy (a filtered rewrite with new hashes and the same author times, or a single squashed commit), and each local branch was reset to it, so a plain rev-list of local master no longer measures the work: Quartz's local master gives 244 for the 12 Oct cutoff where the real history had 246. For these repos the count is the pre-switch line on the private-archive remote (read-only; per the reflog it contains the commit local master pointed at just before its reset) plus every commit on the public branch that is not a copy of one on that line. A public commit is a copy when its author time matches a commit on the private line, one for one (the rewrite kept author times but changed some subjects), or when its tree equals a private commit's tree (a squash). With the 12 Oct cutoff this reproduces 246 for Quartz, 202 for Mantle and 53 for Helm. Helm's private line is private-archive/wk/opensource-prep, which holds its pre-switch master (0f53c26, 16 Oct) and the 22 open-source prep commits that the public squash 2e0668a copies.
The browser is named Quartz; its id stays `browser`.
ISO week keys are %G-W%V (ISO-8601 week-numbering year and week), cross-checked against an independent ISO-week computation for every commit.
all_repos is an extra block (added 2026-10-12) that the site's existing code ignores: commit totals for every repo of Owen's own work on this machine, same cutoff.

all_repos.note: Every git repo of Owen's own work on his machine, counted the same way (author date before 2026-10-26T00:00:00-07:00, i.e. through 25 October local). Site code that reads totals/projects ignores this block. A repo with a single commit dated 2026-09-20 (or 14 Oct) is a backup snapshot: that project was built before it had git history and was pushed once as a private backup, so its count of 1 says nothing about its size.
all_repos.command: git -C <repo> rev-list --count --before=2026-10-26T00:00:00-07:00 <branch>; first/last = git log <branch> --before=... --date=short. Repos published 20-23 Oct: the pre-switch private-archive line plus the new public commits (see _source.notes).
all_repos.branch_rule: Atlas on origin/master (production); every other repo on its checked-out default branch (for the published repos, that branch's pre-switch line on private-archive plus its new public commits).
